## 1. Data Loading & Cleaning

### 1.1 WVS Wave 7

Negative values are proprietary missing codes in the WVS codebook and are recoded to `NA`.
Moral permissiveness items (Q177–Q195) and institutional trust items (Q57–Q62) are retained.

```{r wvs-load}
wvs_raw <- read_csv(
  "/Users/calypsocalcott/Downloads/wvs_wave7/WVS_Cross-National_Wave_7_csv_v6_0.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

moral_items <- paste0("Q", 177:195)
trust_items <- paste0("Q", 57:62)
all_items   <- c(moral_items, trust_items)

wvs <- wvs_raw %>%
  select(country = B_COUNTRY_ALPHA, weight = W_WEIGHT, all_of(all_items)) %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(all_items), ~ if_else(. < 0, NA_real_, as.numeric(.))))

cat(sprintf("WVS: %d respondents across %d countries\n",
            nrow(wvs), n_distinct(wvs$country)))
```

### 1.2 Country-Level Aggregation (Weighted Means)

Items are averaged into four theory-driven moral composites. All means are weighted by the survey design weight (`W_WEIGHT`).

| Composite | Items | Theoretical basis |
|-----------|-------|-------------------|
| **Purity** | Q182, Q183, Q186, Q193 | Moral foundations — sanctity/degradation |
| **Harm** | Q189, Q190, Q191, Q192, Q194 | Moral foundations — care/harm |
| **Fairness** | Q177, Q178, Q179, Q180, Q181 | Moral foundations — fairness/reciprocity |
| **Autonomy** | Q184, Q185, Q187, Q188 | Personal freedom norms |

Higher scores indicate greater permissiveness (scale 1–10 in the raw WVS).

```{r wvs-aggregate}
wvs_country <- wvs %>%
  group_by(country) %>%
  summarise(
    n_wvs = n(),
    across(all_of(all_items), ~ weighted.mean(., w = weight, na.rm = TRUE)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    purity   = rowMeans(select(., Q182, Q183, Q186, Q193),          na.rm = TRUE),
    harm     = rowMeans(select(., Q189, Q190, Q191, Q192, Q194),    na.rm = TRUE),
    fairness = rowMeans(select(., Q177, Q178, Q179, Q180, Q181),    na.rm = TRUE),
    autonomy = rowMeans(select(., Q184, Q185, Q187, Q188),          na.rm = TRUE),
    trust_ip = rowMeans(select(., Q57, Q58, Q59),                   na.rm = TRUE)
  )

cat(sprintf("Country-level dataset: %d countries\n", nrow(wvs_country)))
```

### 1.3 Moral Foundations Questionnaire (YourMorals)

Individual-level MFQ responses from YourMorals.org are aggregated to country means. Only countries with n ≥ 30 respondents are retained. The six MFQ subscales are collapsed into two higher-order scores: **Individualizing** (Care + Equality + Proportionality) and **Binding** (Hierarchy + Loyalty + Purity).

```{r mfq}
mfq_raw <- read_csv(
  "/Users/calypsocalcott/Downloads/MFQ_clean (2).csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

mfq_country <- mfq_raw %>%
  filter(!is.na(currentCountry), currentCountry != "") %>%
  group_by(country = currentCountry) %>%
  summarise(
    n_mfq         = n(),
    mfq_care      = mean(care_score,            na.rm = TRUE),
    mfq_hierarchy = mean(hierarchy_score,       na.rm = TRUE),
    mfq_prop      = mean(proportionality_score, na.rm = TRUE),
    mfq_equality  = mean(equality_score,        na.rm = TRUE),
    mfq_loyalty   = mean(loyalty_score,         na.rm = TRUE),
    mfq_purity    = mean(purity_score,          na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(n_mfq >= 30) %>%
  mutate(
    mfq_individualizing = (mfq_care + mfq_equality + mfq_prop) / 3,
    mfq_binding         = (mfq_hierarchy + mfq_loyalty + mfq_purity) / 3
  )

# Map full country names to ISO3
```

## 2. Analysis

### 2.1 GDP Residualization

Each predictor and outcome is separately regressed on log GDP per capita. Residuals represent variance *not* attributable to national wealth.

```{r residualize}
resid_on_gdp <- function(x, g) {
  ok <- !is.na(x) & !is.na(g)
  r  <- rep(NA_real_, length(x))
  if (sum(ok) >= 5) r[ok] <- residuals(lm(x[ok] ~ g[ok]))
  r
}

df_r <- df %>%
  mutate(across(
    all_of(c(outcomes, predictors)),
    ~ resid_on_gdp(., log_gdp),
    .names = "{.col}_r"
  ))
```

### 2.2 LOO-CV R² (Q²)

Leave-one-out cross-validation R² is computed via the hat-matrix PRESS shortcut, avoiding the need to refit N models:

$$Q^2 = 1 - \frac{\text{PRESS}}{\text{SST}}, \quad \text{PRESS} = \sum_i \left(\frac{e_i}{1-h_{ii}}\right)^2$$

Q² < 0 means the model predicts out-of-sample *worse than the grand mean* — a stringent penalty for overfitting in small samples.

```{r loo-cv}
loo_cv_r2 <- function(y, x) {
  ok <- !is.na(y) & !is.na(x)
  n  <- sum(ok)
  if (n < 6) return(list(r = NA_real_, r2 = NA_real_, q2 = NA_real_, n = n))
  y_ <- y[ok]; x_ <- x[ok]
  fit  <- lm(y_ ~ x_)
  h    <- hatvalues(fit)
  e    <- residuals(fit)
  press <- sum((e / (1 - h))^2)
  sst   <- sum((y_ - mean(y_))^2)
  list(
    r  = cor(y_, x_),
    r2 = summary(fit)$r.squared,
    q2 = 1 - press / sst,
    n  = n
  )
}

results <- expand_grid(outcome = outcomes, predictor = predictors) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    res = list(loo_cv_r2(
      df_r[[paste0(outcome,   "_r")]],
      df_r[[paste0(predictor, "_r")]]
    )),
    r  = res$r,
    r2 = res$r2,
    q2 = res$q2,
    n  = res$n
  ) %>%
  select(-res) %>%
  ungroup()

write_csv(results,
  "/Users/calypsocalcott/LLM_Coordination/wvs_cultural_analysis/results_table.csv")
```

### 2.4 Two-Predictor Models (Top Competitors)

```{r two-predictor}
top2 <- results %>%
  filter(!is.na(q2)) %>%
  group_by(outcome) %>%
  slice_max(q2, n = 2) %>%
  ungroup()

two_pred_results <- map_dfr(outcomes, function(oc) {
  preds <- top2 %>% filter(outcome == oc) %>% pull(predictor)
  if (length(preds) < 2) return(NULL)
  p1v <- paste0(preds[1], "_r")
  p2v <- paste0(preds[2], "_r")
  yv  <- paste0(oc, "_r")
  ok  <- complete.cases(df_r[[yv]], df_r[[p1v]], df_r[[p2v]])
  if (sum(ok) < 6) return(NULL)
  fit   <- lm(df_r[[yv]][ok] ~ df_r[[p1v]][ok] + df_r[[p2v]][ok])
  h     <- hatvalues(fit); e <- residuals(fit)
  press <- sum((e / (1 - h))^2)
  sst   <- sum((df_r[[yv]][ok] - mean(df_r[[yv]][ok]))^2)
  tibble(
    outcome    = oc,
    predictor1 = preds[1],
    predictor2 = preds[2],
    n          = sum(ok),
    q2_joint   = round(1 - press / sst, 3)
  )
})

two_pred_results %>%
  kable(caption = "Joint Q² for top-2 predictor combinations") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"))
```

```{r plot-setup}
pred_labels <- c(
  enke_kinship        = "Enke Kinship\nTightness",

  rel_mobility        = "Relational\nMobility",

  mfq_individualizing = "MFQ\nIndividualizing",
  mfq_binding         = "MFQ\nBinding"
)

  fairness = "Fairness",

)

# Rebuild country-level residualized data for scatter plots
df_scatter <- df %>%
  mutate(across(
    c(purity, harm, fairness, autonomy, enke_kinship, gelfand_tl),

    .names = "{.col}_r"

base_theme <- theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
    plot.subtitle    = element_text(size = 10, color = "grey40"),
    axis.title       = element_text(size = 11),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.border     = element_rect(color = "grey80", fill = NA)

```

### 3.1 Q² Heatmap — Predictive Accuracy by Measure and Moral Domain

```{r plot-heatmap, fig.height=5}
heatmap_data <- results %>%
  filter(!is.na(q2)) %>%
  mutate(
    pred_label = pred_labels[predictor],
    out_label  = outcome_labels[outcome],
    label      = sprintf("%.2f\n(n=%d)", q2, n),
    sig        = case_when(q2 > 0.3 ~ "strong", q2 > 0 ~ "positive", TRUE ~ "negative")
  )

p1 <- ggplot(
  heatmap_data,
  aes(x = factor(pred_label, levels = pred_labels),
      y = factor(out_label,  levels = rev(outcome_labels)),
      fill = q2)
) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_text(aes(label = label), size = 3.2, lineheight = 1.2) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "#d73027", mid = "#ffffbf", high = "#1a9850",
    midpoint = 0, limits = c(-0.35, 0.65),
    name = "LOO-CV R²"
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(position = "top") +
  labs(
    title    = "Predictive Accuracy by Cultural Measure and Moral Domain",
    subtitle = "LOO-CV R² (Q²) after GDP residualization | green = good out-of-sample fit, red = worse than mean",
    x = NULL, y = NULL
  ) +
  base_theme +
  theme(
    axis.text.x     = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
    axis.text.y     = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "right",
    panel.border    = element_blank(),
    panel.grid      = element_blank()
  )

print(p1)
```

### 3.2 Overall Predictor Ranking (Mean Q² Across All Outcomes)

```{r plot-ranking, fig.height=4}
ranking <- results %>%
  group_by(predictor) %>%
  summarise(mean_q2 = mean(q2, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(
    label    = pred_labels[predictor],
    positive = mean_q2 > 0
  ) %>%
  arrange(mean_q2)

p2 <- ggplot(ranking,
             aes(x = mean_q2, y = reorder(label, mean_q2), fill = positive)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.65) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.8, color = "grey30") +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = sprintf("%.3f", mean_q2),
        hjust = if_else(positive, -0.15, 1.15)),
    size = 3.5, fontface = "bold"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "#1a9850", "FALSE" = "#d73027"),
                    guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-0.18, 0.26), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(
    title    = "Overall Predictor Ranking",
    subtitle = "Mean LOO-CV R² averaged across all four moral outcomes",
    x = "Mean LOO-CV R²", y = NULL
  ) +
  base_theme +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())

print(p2)
```

### 3.3 Significant Relationships — Cultural Tightness Predicts Purity and Autonomy

```{r plot-scatter-sig, fig.height=9}
make_scatter <- function(data, x_var, y_var, x_lab, y_lab, title) {
  d     <- data %>% filter(!is.na(.data[[x_var]]), !is.na(.data[[y_var]]))
  r_val <- round(cor(d[[x_var]], d[[y_var]]), 2)
  ggplot(d, aes(x = .data[[x_var]], y = .data[[y_var]], label = country)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "grey70", linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "grey70", linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "#2166ac",
                fill = "#2166ac", alpha = 0.15, linewidth = 1) +
    geom_point(size = 2.2, color = "#2166ac", alpha = 0.8) +
    geom_text_repel(size = 2.8, color = "grey30", max.overlaps = 20,
                    segment.color = "grey70", segment.size = 0.3) +
    annotate("text", x = Inf, y = Inf, hjust = 1.1, vjust = 1.5,
             label = sprintf("r = %s", r_val), fontface = "bold", size = 4) +
    labs(title = title, x = x_lab, y = y_lab) +
    base_theme
}

p3a <- make_scatter(df_scatter, "enke_kinship_r", "purity_r",
  "Enke Kinship Tightness (residualized)",
  "Purity permissiveness (residualized)",
  "Kinship Tightness → Purity  [Q²=0.58]")

p3b <- make_scatter(df_scatter, "gelfand_tl_r", "purity_r",
  "Gelfand Tightness-Looseness (residualized)",
  "Purity permissiveness (residualized)",
  "Tightness-Looseness → Purity  [Q²=0.51]")

p3c <- make_scatter(df_scatter, "enke_kinship_r", "autonomy_r",
  "Enke Kinship Tightness (residualized)",
  "Autonomy permissiveness (residualized)",
  "Kinship Tightness → Autonomy  [Q²=0.27]")

p3d <- make_scatter(df_scatter, "gelfand_tl_r", "autonomy_r",
  "Gelfand Tightness-Looseness (residualized)",
  "Autonomy permissiveness (residualized)",
  "Tightness-Looseness → Autonomy  [Q²=0.29]")

p3 <- (p3a | p3b) / (p3c | p3d) +
  plot_annotation(
    title    = "Cultural Tightness Predicts Purity and Autonomy Attitudes",
    subtitle = "GDP-residualized values; axes show variance not explained by national wealth",

      plot.title    = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10, color = "grey40")
    )
  )

print(p3)
```

## 4. Summary

```{r summary-table}
results %>%
  group_by(predictor) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_q2    = round(mean(q2, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    max_q2     = round(max(q2, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    n_positive = sum(q2 > 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_outcomes = sum(!is.na(q2)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(mean_q2)) %>%
  mutate(label = pred_labels[predictor]) %>%
  select(Measure = label, `Mean Q2` = mean_q2, `Max Q2` = max_q2,
         `Outcomes > 0` = n_positive, `Outcomes tested` = n_outcomes) %>%
  kable(caption = "Predictor performance summary") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover")) %>%
  row_spec(1, bold = TRUE, background = "#e8f5e9")
```

**Key findings:**

- **Enke kinship tightness** is the strongest overall predictor (mean Q² = 0.18), driven by large effects on Purity (Q² = 0.58) and Autonomy (Q² = 0.27).
- **Gelfand tightness-looseness** performs similarly on Purity (Q² = 0.51) and Autonomy (Q² = 0.29) but covers fewer countries (N ≈ 18–19).
- **Harm and Fairness** show no positive Q² for any predictor after GDP residualization — cross-national variation in these domains appears to be driven primarily by national wealth, not cultural tightness.
- **MFQ scores** (Individualizing and Binding) derived from YourMorals convenience samples fail to predict WVS moral attitudes; mean Q² < 0 for both.
- **Relational mobility** and **interpersonal trust** show modest, inconsistent predictive value.
